newsitem.title: USA: CBOT adds 12 candidates to annual election ballot.
newsitem.headline: CBOT adds 12 candidates to annual election ballot.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade said 12 petition candidates were added to its ballot for the annual exchange election which will be held Dec 11.
John Gilmore was petitioned to run for the two-year term of chairman of the board of directors opposite incumbent chairman Patrick Arbor.
Gilmore, who was CBOT chairman in 1986, has been a member of the exchange since 1967 and is a limited partner at Goldman, Sachs & Co.

Dale Lorenzen, vice president of Merrill Lynch Futures Inc's grain division, and Peter Todebush, incumbent second vice chairman and general partner with Jackson Associates, were added to the slate for second vice chairman.
The CBOT's nominating committee selected Richard Sandor, chairman and CEO of Centre Financial Products Ltd to run as second vice chairman.
For the three-year term of full member director, incumbent Ann Berg, who is an independent trader, and Michael Daley, senior vice president with PaineWebber, were added.
Harold Richard, president/CEO of Farmers Commodities Corp (FCC) in West Des Moines, Iowa, was included to run as non-resident full member director.

Incumbent Paul Johnson, who is vice president of Quantum Financial Services Inc, Jerome Sullivan, an independent trader with Eagle Market Makers Inc, and Jay Vanerstrom, general partner of Jackson Associates, were included to run for the three-year term of associate member director.

Richard Durra, owner of Durra Grain Co and former full member director from 1993 to 1995, and Jerry Manne, president of Alaska Commodities Inc, were added to the ballot to run as full members on the CBOT's nominating committee.
James Baer, an independent trader who has been a CBOT member since 1979, will run for the two-year associate member positions on the CBOT's nominating committee.
